_note: Finished goods between a raw material and a household need or a producer's capital (Complaints/533): nails and roof tiles. Each has a maker recipe here and users named in its yield_basis.

nails_kg.basis: per kg of hand-forged iron nails
nails_kg.yield_basis: MEAN NAIL: the Inchtuthil hoard is 875,400 hand-forged nails 'in four sizes, weighing approximately seven tonnes' (ANU Classics Museum catalogue, https://slll.cass.anu.edu.au/classics-museum/catalogue/objects/five-roman-nails-201214, opened), so a mean nail is about 8 g; five sampled nails run 3.0 g to 212.5 g, 63 to 260 mm. It fixes the unit (a kilogram is about 125 nails), not the bar or the hours. BAR: 1.1 kg of bar a kilogram of nails (scale loss and cut-off heads) is a LABELLED HEURISTIC, conf D; retire: Complaints/533. Pass 12 searched again: Blacksmiths Depot (https://www.blacksmithsdepot.com/nail_heading, seen in a search result, not opened) and the Monticello pages (403 on monticello.org; daacs.org, https://www.daacs.org/?p=194, opened) say only that Jefferson recorded each nailer's rod waste, with no percentage; the Historical Metallurgy Society paper on the Monticello nailery (Abdu, Gordon and Knopf, hmsjournal.org, opened as text) gives no loss ratio. No source found for the figure. HOURS (Pass 11, value changed from 12 to 2 smith hours a kilogram): Kenneth Schwarz in Mortise and Tenon Magazine issue 15 (https://mortiseandtenonmag.com/blogs/blog/issue-15-t-o-c-kenneth-schwarz-accustomed-to-handle-the-hammer-the-nail-making-specialty-in-pre-industrial-manufacture, opened) says 'dedicated nailers could average around 200 nails per hour'; the SPACO page below gives 87 and 230 an hour; a search summary of an economics paper citing Rybczynski put it near one nail a minute (60 an hour, not opened). At the 8 g mean nail, 60 to 230 nails an hour is 0.5 to 1.8 kg an hour, 0.55 to 2.1 hours a kilogram; 2 is taken at the slow end because the mean is pulled up by a few large nails and rod preparation is included. The 12 hours implied 10 nails an hour, 6 to 20 times slower than every figure found. Opened and not sufficient: the French Creek Valley (SPACO) page 'Making Hand Forged Nails' (https://www.spaco.org/Blacksmithing/Nails/Nailmaking.htm, revised October 2023) reports a demonstrator's best of 87 nails an hour and a smith who could do 230 an hour, nail size not stated; at the mean 8 g nail above that would be well under 12 hours a kilogram, so 12 is probably high, but without the nail size no hours-per-kilogram can be derived. USERS: carts (data/production/99_carriers.json) and timber frames (97_building_services.json). Round 4 (Pass 14) rod loss: Jefferson's Farm Book page 110 (https://dasfam.monticello.org/documents/farmbook_page110.html, opened): 'the ton of rod is 2240', 'common loss 14. pr ct', 'nails yeilded 1926', so a kilogram of nails takes 1 / 0.86 = 1.16 kg of rod (was 1.1, within 3x; changed to the sourced figure). Cross-check: Sedgley Manor, nailmakers (https://sedgleymanor.com/trades/nailmakers2.html, opened): a 60 lb bundle of rod returned 'as much as 52lb with 8lb waste' for large nails (60 / 52 = 1.15), and the union asked 'Add 12lbs. of iron to make 10lbs. of nails' (1.2). Hours were already sourced above.

roof_tile_kg.basis: per kg of fired clay roof tile
roof_tile_kg.yield_basis: A roof tile is fired earthenware (ceramic_kg's basis names tile). BREAKAGE: 1.05 kg of fired ware a kilogram of laid tile, and 0.1 potter hour a kilogram of extra moulding and trimming beyond the ware's own hours, are LABELLED HEURISTICS, conf D; retire: Complaints/533. Pass 12 on the breakage: Studio Matrx, Roof Tile Calculator (https://www.studiomatrx.org/utilities/roof-tile-calculator, opened): 'Clay tiles break in handling & laying; 5-10% is typical, more for country tiles', default allowance 10 percent; the 1.05 here is the low end of that range and kept (within 2x of the 1.10 top). The 0.1 potter hours have no source. No weight of a whole Roman tegula or imbrex was found: the Wessex Archaeology Dorchester report (wessexarch.co.uk, 13_Ceramic_build_mat.pdf, opened) tabulates imbrex and tegula sherds by count and weight only, which says nothing about a whole tile. USERS: brick and stone walls, which are roofed in tile (97_building_services.json). Round 4 (Pass 14) tried: rate from a trade page (Practical Action, Clay tile manufacture, https://rachel.core2learn.org/modules/en-practical_action/Construction/Roofing%20and%20flooring/clay_tile_manufacture.pdf, opened with pdftotext: a powered pugmill and two presses make up to 7,000 tiles a day, with a crew of presses, shelvers and a pug-mill feeder, which is machine work and does not bound hand moulding), a 1916 trade note on hand-operated concrete tile machines (150 to 250 tiles per man per day, concrete, search summary only), a search for hand-moulded plain tile output per day (none). Missing: tiles per hand-moulder per day and the tile mass, to turn into hours per kilogram.
